label: French Cuff — 4 Buttonholes

profile.distinguishingDetail: A French cuff with four buttonholes is the conventional double-cuff arrangement, with two aligned holes on each leaf so a single cufflink passes cleanly through all four layers when folded. This is the standard cufflink closure and produces the familiar crisp, squared double cuff that frames the cufflink neatly. It offers a slightly cleaner, more traditional look than higher buttonhole counts while retaining full formality.

ownerReferences.evidence: Real photograph (208x260 px) of a worn pale-blue shirt cuff held between thumb and fingers. A second fabric layer peeks past the wrist edge beside the thumb, consistent with a folded-back double cuff. Because the fastened cufflink covers the holes, ZERO buttonholes are countable - 4 vs 6 vs 8 cannot be distinguished.
